name: MAX6675
full_name: Maxim Integrated (Analog Devices) MAX6675 Cold-Junction-Compensated K-Thermocouple-to-Digital Converter (0C to +1024C)
description: The MAX6675 performs cold-junction compensation and digitizes the signal from a type-K thermocouple. It outputs 12-bit data with 0.25 C resolution over a read-only SPI-compatible interface, covering 0 C to +1024 C. The device includes built-in open-thermocouple detection, flagging a disconnected probe in the data word. Because it integrates the cold-junction sensing, ADC, and reference, it turns a bare thermocouple into a clean digital temperature reading with minimal external parts. It is a long-standing favorite for reflow ovens, kilns, and industrial temperature monitoring.

pins.name: T-
pins.description: Alumel lead of type-K thermocouple; connect to ground externally

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Positive supply; bypass with 0.1 uF to GND

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select; set low to enable the serial interface and latch a reading

typical_application: Reading a K-type thermocouple temperature into a microcontroller for reflow ovens, kilns, or process control.
gotchas: Read-only interface: there is no data-input (MOSI/DIN) pin; you only clock 16 bits out on SO, no commands are written
T- (pin 2) must be tied to ground externally; floating it gives garbage readings
Bit D2 of the 16-bit word is the open-thermocouple flag; always check it before trusting a reading
Thermocouple polarity matters: chromel to T+ (pin 3), alumel to T- (pin 2); swapping reads backwards
Cold-junction (ambient at the chip) is only valid from -20 C to +85 C, so keep the IC away from the hot zone
VCC minimum is 3.0 V; do not run it at the 2.6-2.7 V floor common to the other converters here
The pin-compatible MAX31855 is the modern successor with wider range and SPI; do not assume identical data format
